title: Flat-band formation and chiral superconductivity in driven topological insulators
authors: Suman Jyoti De, Leo Goutte, Kartiek Agarwal, T. Pereg-Barnea
abstract: We demonstrate that circularly polarized light can be used to Floquet-engineer nearly flat or Mexican-hat like electronic bands on the surface of three-dimensional topological insulators (3D TIs), which under suitable conditions, can support topological superconductivity via purely repulsive Coulomb interactions. The driving acts not merely by gapping out the Dirac cone on the surface of the 3D TI, but can be used to diminish, and even flip in sign, the intrinsic curvature of the surface state dispersion away from the Dirac point. Using parameters for canonical 3D TIs, we find that the flat band limit is attained for reasonable electric fields and the bands realized by changing the strength of the driving field have a similar energetic and spatial profile to those obtained in rhombohedral graphene under varying displacement field, where the case for superconductivity with purely repulsive interactions has recently been made. We find that, with the aid of appropriately placed screening metallic gate, one can obtain $T_c \sim 7 $K in this setup while avoiding Wigner crystallization for low electron densities in the range of $10^{11}-10^{12}/\text{cm}^2$.
summary: The paper shows that using circularly polarized light can engineer flat electronic bands on topological insulators. This engineered flatness allows for the emergence of chiral topological superconductivity driven by repulsive Coulomb interactions. The theoretical framework predicts measurable superconducting critical temperatures under realistic conditions.
main_problem: The study demonstrates how circularly polarized light can engineer flat electronic bands on topological insulators to induce chiral superconductivity using purely repulsive Coulomb interactions.
main_result: Topological superconductivity with a critical temperature of $T_c \sim 7$ K is predicted in the relevant density regime ($10^{11}-10^{12}/	ext{cm}^2$) while avoiding Wigner crystallization.
method: The analysis employs Floquet theory to derive an effective time-independent Hamiltonian, followed by solving a mean-field self-consistency equation for the superconducting order parameter using RPA approximations.
model_or_system: The system is the surface states of 3D Topological Insulators (TIs) driven by high-frequency, circularly polarized light. The physics is modeled via an effective Floquet Hamiltonian and treated with screened Coulomb interactions.
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), superconducting order parameter ($\Delta(\vec{k})$ or $\eta_\ell(k)$), and the gas parameter ($r_s$).
important_parameters: Driving field amplitude ($E_0$), electron density ($n$), gate separation ($d_{	ext{reg}}$), and the flat-band condition ($E_0 \approx E_{	ext{flat}}^0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on projecting interactions into a single lower Floquet band, and approximations are made regarding projection factors in the interaction Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the engineered flat-band dispersion (Mexican-hat shape), phase diagrams showing $T_c$ dependence on density/drive amplitude, and the superconducting order parameter profile for different driving strengths.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the Floquet engineering of flat bands, then calculating the effective screened interaction via RPA, and finally solving the self-consistent mean-field equations to determine the chiral superconducting pairing ($\ell=\pm 1$) and $T_c$.
why_interesting: This work directly connects concepts from quantum optics (Floquet driving) and condensed matter theory (topological materials, superconductivity) to realize exotic correlated states in a controllable platform.
